subject: Banking
title: Stablecoins and Shadow Banking
description: A 60-second lesson on Stablecoins and Shadow Banking.

hook.text: Tether processes more daily volume than Visa. A stablecoin pegged to the US dollar moves more money than the largest.

buildup.text: Stablecoins are crypto tokens designed to maintain a fixed value, usually $1.

discovery.text: Tether claims each token is backed by reserves. But audits have been incomplete, raising questions about real backing.

twist.text: TerraUSD, an algorithmic stablecoin, collapsed in 2022. It lost its peg and destroyed $40 billion in value in 48 hours.

climax.text: Stablecoins are unregulated banks in disguise. They take deposits and promise redemption, with no deposit insurance.

punchline.text: More volume than Visa. No deposit insurance. Stablecoins are shadow banks.

quiz.question: What happened to the TerraUSD stablecoin?
options: It lost its dollar peg and destroyed $40 billion in 48 hours
It was acquired by a bank

details.summary: Stablecoins are digital tokens pegged to currencies like the dollar, operating as private money outside the traditional banking system. Their rapid growth creates shadow banking risks because they function like bank deposits without deposit insurance.
details.whyItMatters: Stablecoins hold over 130 billion dollars in reserves but operate outside banking regulation. If a major stablecoin loses its peg, the resulting panic could create a bank-run-like event in the crypto ecosystem with potential spillover to traditiona.
takeaways: Stablecoins hold over 130 billion dollars and function like digital dollars
They provide deposit-like services without FDIC insurance or bank regulation
Tether's reserve composition has been a persistent source of concern

faq.question: What happens if a stablecoin loses its peg?
faq.answer: TerraUSD's collapse in 2022 showed the devastating consequences: 40 billion dollars evaporated in days, triggering a cascade of crypto failures. A similar collapse of Tether or USDC would be far more damaging given their larger scale and broader use.

faq.question: Should stablecoins be regulated like banks?
faq.answer: Many regulators think so. Stablecoins perform bank-like functions of holding and transferring value. Proposed regulations would require stablecoin issuers to hold full reserves in safe assets and submit to bank-like examination and reporting.
